name: Jinqi Jiangtang (traditional Chinese herbal formula)
short: Report review: products with its herb Coptis (formula not named) linked to arrhythmia with mianserin, other antidepressant reactions. China diabetes trials: adverse events, low sugar not more common.
text: Safety data on Jinqi Jiangtang tablets, a formula of three herbs (Coptis chinensis, Astragalus membranaceus and Lonicera japonica), are thin and come from trials conducted in China. A 2019 meta-analysis of 17 randomised trials in 1,425 people with type 2 diabetes found no statistical difference between the tablets added to conventional therapy and conventional therapy alone in the total incidence of adverse events or in the incidence of hypoglycaemia (low blood sugar), and the authors said the results should be interpreted with caution; the abstract does not describe which adverse events occurred. An overview of meta-analyses of 18 plant-based remedies for glucose control in type 2 diabetes, which included this formula, reported no serious adverse effects across the remedies, without giving figures for this formula. A 2019 review of the formula said its quality control system is not perfect and its clinical applications need to be re-evaluated. For one of its herbs, Coptis chinensis, a retrospective review of adverse event reports linked products containing it, taken together with antidepressants, to arrhythmias (with mianserin), swelling of the lower limbs and muscle pain (with mirtazapine) and breast enlargement (with fluoxetine); the abstract does not name the products or say whether any was this formula, so these reports are not direct evidence about Jinqi Jiangtang, and they are the only interaction data found in the cited sources.
